text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said the outlook for the region remains promising compared to last year when tension over the Taiwan straits between the United States and China threatened to mar stability in the area.
- Singapore's economy should improve in 1997 following growth in the U.S. economy and marginally better economic conditions in Europe, said Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
- The chief executive of NTUC Income, Tan Kin Lian, said their firm is studying the possibility of importing cars to compete with authorised agents by selling them at lower prices to the public.
- Users of the outdated analog AMPS cellular phone system will have to wait at least another year to be upgraded to a newer digital network because of a delay in the tender selection process.
- The Goei family, one of Singapore's leading property developers until it diversified in the late 1980s, is developing its first hotel in Australia's Queensland state.

- British airways and Australia-based Qantas expect to enjoy this year the fruits of their marketing and operational alliance in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, said the regional general manager for the arrangement, Ian Gay.
- Rents for prime retail space in Singapore's Orchard Road will probably hold steady for another year despite protracted weakness in the retail market, property consultant Richard Ellis said.
- Hong Kong's economy will continue to remain buoyant after it reverts to China in July, provided the mainland continues to prosper, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said.
- Singapore's general insurance industry will go through a placid phase this year with slower premium growth and increasing loss ratios, the Asia Insurance Review said.

- The number of piracy cases rose to 175 in 1996 from 170 the previous year and the attacks have become increasingly violent, the Kuala Lumpur-based International Maritime Bureau Regional Piracy Centre said in its annual report.
- Singapore and Hong Kong are locked in fierce competition to woo a growing number of Taiwanese companies seeking listings on foreign stock exchanges.
